behavioral_notes.observation: event.sponsor is a per-event exhibitor/sponsor record that inherits website.published.mixin + website.searchable.mixin, so each booth is an independently publishable web page. _compute_website_url overrides the mixin so website_url points at /event/<event-slug>/exhibitor/<sponsor-slug>. exhibitor_type is a Selection [sponsor='Footer Logo Only', exhibitor='Exhibitor', online='Online Exhibitor']: only 'exhibitor'/'online' get a booth in the directory (the listing/search base domain filters exhibitor_type in ['exhibitor','online']), while 'sponsor' is footer-logo-only and excluded. The model lazily mirrors name/email/phone/image_512/website_description/url from partner_id via _synchronize_with_partner / _compute_* but never writes back to the partner (values are treated as event-specific). show_on_ticket drives the report bundle. This published-booth + partner-mirror behaviour is pure code, invisible to metadata.

event.sponsor.type is a standalone catalog of sponsorship tiers (name translatable, sequence auto-incremented by _default_sequence, display_ribbon_style Selection no_ribbon/Gold/Silver/Bronze). event.sponsor.sponsor_type_id defaults to the highest-sequence type and is required; the exhibitors directory groups booths by sponsor_type_id and sorts (sponsor_type_id.sequence, sequence), so the tier drives both the on-page grouping/heading and the ribbon badge. event.event._compute_sponsor_count exposes sponsor_count via a _read_group. Tier semantics live entirely in Python/data, not in the schema.

ExhibitorController extends WebsiteEventController. /event/<id>/exhibitors (alias /exhibitor) renders website_event_exhibitor.event_exhibitors: it builds search_domain from _get_event_sponsors_base_domain (event_id + exhibitor_type in [exhibitor,online]; AND is_published=True unless the user is in event.group_event_registration_desk), adds free-text (name/website_description ilike), country (partner_id.country_id) and sponsorship-level facets, then groups sorted booths by sponsor_type_id and randomises within each tier (published booths first via sample() for desk users). The detail route /event/<id>/exhibitor/<sponsor> is matched only when event.exhibitor_menu=True, calls sponsor.has_access('read') (Forbidden otherwise) then sudo()s, renders event_exhibitor_main, and builds a 'sponsors_other' sidebar sorted by website_published, is_in_opening_hours, same-country, -sponsor_type sequence and a random tiebreaker. The event.event gains an 'Exhibitors list' website.event.menu (menu_type 'exhibitor') at /event/<slug>/exhibitors via _get_website_menu_entries. None of this routing/search/sort logic is in metadata.

is_in_opening_hours is a TZ-aware compute keyed on event_id.is_ongoing and hour_from/hour_to: it localises now/date_begin/date_end into event.date_tz, clamps the booth's opening window to the event window, and returns True only while the booth is currently live (with a midnight=next-day special case). This drives the live 'Connect'/'meet the sponsor' UX: the ExhibitorConnect public.interaction (.o_wesponsor_connect_button) reads data-event-is-ongoing/data-sponsor-is-ongoing/data-user-event-manager and either redirects to the sponsor URL when live, or opens the ExhibitorConnectClosedDialog OWL component. That dialog rpc-fetches /event_sponsor/<id>/read (jsonrpc, public) which marshals sponsor + sponsor_type + event timing (is_ongoing/is_done/start_remaining, formatted hours) for the 'event not started / sponsor not available' modal. The availability/connect logic is split across the Python compute and the JS interaction, outside metadata.

3 JS files / 2 XML templates, one OWL component (ExhibitorConnectClosedDialog, extends web Dialog) and one website public.interaction (website_event_exhibitor.exhibitor_connect); no registry patches. The interaction debounces the connect-button click (500ms) and routes to redirect() vs. the closed-info dialog based on live state; the dialog lazily rpc-loads sponsor data and renders a luxon-formatted countdown to event start. Assets: web.assets_frontend (4 entries incl. exhibitor scss/templates), web.report_assets_common (full-page ticket report css, tied to show_on_ticket) and website.website_builder_assets (event_page_option editor snippet). Entirely client-side / static, outside Python metadata.

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_event_exhibitor is a value network (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating technology): it exists to connect two populations -- sponsors/exhibitors and event attendees -- on the event website. It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve case-by-case problems (shop); its economic logic is mediation/matching. It extends website_event (itself the network bridge that fuses website + event) by adding a publishable exhibitor booth (event.sponsor on website.published.mixin), a sponsorship-tier catalog (event.sponsor.type), and the public /event/<id>/exhibitors directory + /exhibitor/<sponsor> booth pages whose whole purpose is to let attendees find and reach sponsors -- including a live, opening-hours-gated 'Connect / meet the sponsor' action (redirect to sponsor URL or a not-available modal via /event_sponsor/<id>/read). That is membership/contact mediation between an open set of exhibitors and attendees. activity_class is primary because exhibitor showcasing & engagement is a customer-facing event-marketing demand activity, not back-office support. apqc_category 3.0 Market and Sell is the closest PCF home, inherited from website_event/event: the motion is promoting sponsors and engaging attendees around a marketed event (sponsor visibility, lead/contact generation), not 6.0 post-sale customer service; strategy is left null (human).
